metadata.title: Network security incident investigation
metadata.artifact_scope_note: Evidence is aggregated query output (not raw packets); it contains no chat/communication records.

incident_description: Network security investigation of a monitored LAN. Evidence consists of Elasticsearch aggregation results over Zeek and Suricata logs (IDS alerts, Kerberos, HTTP downloads, TLS certificates, domains and external-destination activity). No root cause, impact or C2 attribution is stated; these must be established from the supplied artifacts. Network context: LAN segment range: 10.10.22.0/24 (10.10.22.0 through 10.10.22.255); Domain: enemywatch.net; Domain Controller: 10.10.22.22 - ENEMYWATCH-DC; LAN segment gateway: 10.10.22.1; LAN segment broadcast address: 10.10.22.255.
investigation_questions: What are the IP addresses of the potentially infected internal hosts in the LAN?
What are the hostnames of the potentially infected machines in the LAN?
What are the Windows human user account names (not machine accounts ending in $) of the potentially infected machines in the LAN?
What external servers (domains and IP addresses) were used to download malicious files?
What are the suspicious external IP addresses contacted, which might be involved in command-and-control (C2) communication?
What specific malicious file was downloaded by an internal host from multiple external IP addresses?
During what hour did the first signs of infection activity appear? Provide the earliest date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC format.
According to the connection volume statistics, what single external IP address received the most connections from the infected hosts? Is it a C2 server or a legitimate service?
